cards.title: The pattern: hub, thesis, write and read paths
items: Why LLM Wikis Beat RAG is the thesis: synthesis moves to ingest time, so knowledge compounds instead of being re-derived per query, and the economics are about maintenance rather than retrieval.
Three-Layer Architecture is the hub and the shape that makes the thesis safe: immutable raw/, an agent-owned wiki/, and a schema that disciplines the agent.

Ingest Workflow is the write path, one source per session with the user in the loop. Progressive Disclosure is the read side: metadata and index.md route an agent to the right pages but are not where it reasons.

cards.title: Comparators: each tests one piece
items: Skill Evolution (WikiSkill) swaps documents for execution traces and skills for the schema, and supplies the only controlled evidence for compounding: 63.7% with a compiled wiki against 48.7% without, from one paper and one model.
Belief Ledger (gbrain) asks what markdown plus git fails to record, belief history rather than file history, and files that as a property of the wiki layer rather than a fourth layer.

Provenance Tags sets obsidian-wiki's origin tags and OpenWiki's versioned evidence ranges against this KB's claim callouts. Unattended Agent State takes Anthropic's scheduled daily brief as the discipline a timer-driven /scout would need.
Every comparator so far changes the gate, not the layers.

cards.title: Where the tensions are
items: Interactive gate vs mechanical maintenance: Ingest Workflow keeps ingest interactive; the maintenance-economics claim rests on OpenWiki and WikiSkill, which maintain with no human at ingest. Filed as speculative: one-source-per-session is a choice of gate, not of scale.

Who reads the wiki: WikiSkill measured that giving the executing agent wiki access lowered skill quality (63.7% to 60.9%), which sits awkwardly with the read-time-asset premise. The result does not decide who should read a wiki that trains nothing.

Index as replacement for embeddings: the thesis leans on index-first navigation; obsidian-wiki's measurement (44% vs 83% on graph questions) shows the index misleads reasoning and is a routing aid only.
Inference lint cannot see prose: origin-mark lint only counts inference the agent admitted to; the low-confidence 'bookkeeping lapse makes a wiki worse than RAG' line is the kind of claim that hides.

cards.title: Sourcing
items: One paper carries the thesis: everything resting on WikiSkill is medium confidence from one paper, one model, three runs. obsidian-wiki's '2000 pages, same cost' is asserted, not shown.
A second controlled study on a document corpus would move the compounding claim most.
Fractal Federation and Subtractive Onboarding describe the template, not the sources: no sources, no callouts.
Strongest: the hub and the write path, both high confidence. Everything the comparators add is medium.

cards.title: How this differs from The Machinery
items: This map is what the sources say about the pattern; The Machinery is how this KB implements it.
This KB differs from the comparators on the gate: it keeps a human at ingest where WikiSkill, obsidian-wiki and OpenWiki run batch or CI.
